text:
leah: quick question for the group — we're debating whether to do global attribute propagation by default or make certain attr groups opt-in per service. main concern is cost attribution leakage vs instrumentation ergonomics.

sam: can you spell out the two sides? like what "global" would carry that opt-in wouldn't?

leah: sure. global = every service includes full billing/context attrs (tenant_id, customer_tier, cost_key, region_hint) on traces/spans automatically. opt-in = services explicitly declare which attr groups to attach.

kevin: global wins on developer experience and immediate cost visibility. downside is higher cardinality and ingest cost for traces/metrics.

maria: opt-in reduces noise but we risk inconsistent attribution if teams forget to opt in. that led to missing billing for a month last time. :grimacing:

leah: exactly. also privacy/regulatory: some teams can't surface tenant identifiers to our hosted telemetry pipeline, so opt-in helps with policy compliance.

sam: what about a middle ground — default minimal surface (service_id, env) + an allowlist for teams that opt into full attribution? opt-in by default but with a safe, low-friction path to opt in.

tanya: +1. maybe provide a shim in our SDKs: `attachBillingAttrs()` that warns if used in hosted path vs private deployments. deprecate auto-propagation.

kevin: think we also need a rollout playbook. detection: if a service opts out but query patterns show large cost delta, we alert owners to a potential miss.

infra-bot: deploy status: instrumentation-shim @ stage deployed to canary (ci/1223) :white_check_mark:

maria: two implementation notes: 1) have a lightweight attribute envelope so we can drop high-card attrs before storage; 2) keep billing key resolvable via lookup if missing (best-effort) so queries don't hard fail.

leah: proposal: default minimal attrs + SDK opt-in helpers + console flag to mark a service "billing-authorized" which unlocks auto-attach for that service. plus monitoring rule to detect "likely un-attributed" workloads.

sam: TL;DR of tradeoffs for RFC follow-up: (1) DX vs cost, (2) privacy/compliance, (3) detection/remediation complexity.

kevin: agree. add: operational cost of support when teams forget to opt in. that was ~3x eng-hours last quarter.

tanya: can we prototype the SDK shim in a single repo and run a 2-week pilot with billing/cust-eng teams?

leah: yes. action items: 1) kevin to draft RFC appendix with rollout playbook and monitoring rules (due Fri), 2) tanya to prototype SDK helper (POC branch by Wed), 3) sam/maria to define minimal attr set and envelope spec.

maria: I'll start the envelope spec — thinking `envelope.version`, `envelope.provenance`, and `envelope.buckets` for high-card attrs.

kevin: ping me if you want numbers on ingest delta per attr — I can run a quick sim.

leah: thanks everyone. leaving notes here for follow-up in RFC thread. :heart:
